title: 1953 AHSME Problem 10
statement: The number of revolutions of a wheel, with fixed center and with an outside diameter of \(6\) feet, required to cause a point on the rim to go one mile is:

solutions.text:
The wheel’s circumference is \(6\pi\) feet, so the required number of revolutions is \[ \frac{5280}{6\pi}=\frac{880}{\pi}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: In one revolution the rim point travels one circumference
Divide \(5280\) feet by the circumference \(6\pi\) feet
